Sosyal medya üzerinde, pandemi döneminde aşıların yaygınlaştırılmasıyla birlikte morg işçilerinin "gizli kan pıhtıları" bulduğu iddialar dolaşımda. Bu iddialar, aşılamayla ilgili anormal kan pıhtılarının oluşumu arasında neden-sonuç ilişkisi olduğunu öne sürerek aşı güvenliği ve kamu sağlığı önlemleri hakkında endişeler yaratıyor.

Bu iddiaların geçerliliğini değerlendirmek için, morg işçilerinin rolü, kan pıhtılarının oluşumu ve bu raporların pandemi sonrası ortamda nasıl ortaya çıktığına dair bilgiye ihtiyaç vardır.

Morg İşçilerinin Rolü ve Kan Pıhtıları  
Morg işçileri, cenaze törenlerine hazırlık yapmak amacıyla görev yapan profesyonellerdir. Bu işler sırasında, kan dolaşım sisteminde kan pıhtılarının oluşumu, işlerinin bir parçası olarak sıkça görülmektedir. Ölüm sonrası kan doğal olarak pıhtılaşmaya başlar ve ölüm ile morg işçiliği arasında uzun bir süre geçmesi durumunda büyük pıhtılar oluşabilir. Ayrıca, parçalanma süreci kanın konsistansını ve damar içeriklerini de etkileyebilir.

"Yabancı Kan Pıhtıları" Raporları Arka Planı  
"Yabancı kan pıhtıları" ile ilgili raporlar, 2022 yılında küresel olarak COVID-19 aşı kampanyaları sırasında sosyal medya ve bazı alternatif medya kanallarında başlamıştır. Bazı morg işçileri, daha önceki yıllarda görülmeyen büyük, lastikçi ya da lifli yapıda pıhtılar bulduğunu belirtmiştir. Bu anekdot raporlar, aşı skeptik gruplar tarafından alındıktan sonra yayılmaya devam etmiştir. Bu gruplar bazen pıhtıların resimlerini ya da morg işçilerinin beyanlarını da ekleyerek bu iddiaları desteklemiştir.

Bilimsel ve Tıbbi Analiz  
Bu iddialara dair bilimsel uzmanlar ve patolojistler yorumda bulunmuştur. Kan pıhtılaması, altta yatan sağlık sorunları, ilaçlar, hareketsizlik ya da enfeksiyon gibi birçok faktörün etkisiyle oluşabilir. COVID-19, bazı hastalarda kan pıhtıları ve damar komplikasyonlarını artırmaktadır, bu durum özellikle bu hastalardan ölenlerde geçerlidir. Ölümden sonra pıhtı oluşumu, bilimsel olarak doğrulanmış bir fenomen olup, ölüm şekli ve morg işçiliği sürecine kadar geçen süreye göre farklılık gösterebilir.

Şu anda, COVID-19 aşılarının, cesetlerde görülen anormal kan pıhtılarının oluşumuna neden olduğu iddiası için bilimsel bir konsensüs veya dergiye kabul edilen araştırmalar bulunmamaktadır. Büyük sağlık kurumları, kan pıhtılaması ve bazı COVID-19 aşıları (özellikle adenovirüs vektör aşılarıyla ilişkili nadir görülen trombositopenik tromboz sendromu gibi durumlar) ile ilgili endişeleri incelemiştir. Ancak bu olaylar çok nadir olup farklı klinik özelliklere sahiptir.

Gerçekleştirmek İçin Analiz  
"Kovid-19 aşılarının uygulanmasıyla birlikte morg işçilerinin 'yabancı kan pıhtıları' bulduğu" iddiası, sistematik verilere dayanmayan anekdot ifadeler üzerine kuruludur. Aşılama oranlarıyla doğrudan ilişkili olarak cesetlerdeki kan pıhtılarının sıklığı ya da doğası hakkında herhangi bir değişimin olduğu kanıt bulunmamaktadır. Uzmanlar, morg işçilerinin işlem sırasında pıhtıların görünmesinin normal bir olay olduğunu ve bu durumun aşılamayla ilişkisi olmayan birçok faktörle ilişkili olduğunu vurgulamaktadırlar.

Sonuç  
Bazı morg işçileri, COVID-19 aşılarının yaygınlaştırılmasıyla birlikte anormal pıhtılar bulduğunu ve bunları bu aşılamayla ilişkilendirdiğini belirtmiştir. Ancak bu iddiaların doğruluğu için bilimsel bir kanıt bulunmamaktadır. Kan pıhtıları, birçok biyolojik ve çevresel faktörün etkisiyle oluşmaktadır ve cesetlerdeki pıhtıların varlığı, aşı zararının kanıtı olmamaktadır. Bu nedenle, bu iddia bilimsel araştırmalar ve uzmanlar arasında konsensüs bulamamıştır.

Scientific analysis confirms no evidence connects vaccines to unusual clots in corpses, with health agencies emphasizing rare vaccine-related clotting events have distinct clinical profiles.

article_content:
A claim circulating on social media states that Denmark has “banned COVID-19 vaccines for anyone under 50.” This statement has caused confusion and concern among the public, prompting questions about the accuracy of the claim and the policies behind Denmark’s COVID-19 vaccination program.

To assess the truth of this claim, it is important to understand the context of Denmark’s approach to COVID-19 vaccination, particularly as the pandemic entered a new phase and the majority of the population had already been vaccinated or exposed to the virus.

In September 2022, Danish health authorities announced a change in their COVID-19 vaccination strategy ahead of the fall and winter seasons. Rather than maintaining a broad, population-wide campaign, Denmark shifted to a more targeted approach, focusing on those most at risk of severe illness from COVID-19. Specifically, the autumn booster program was offered primarily to people aged 50 and above, as well as individuals considered at higher risk due to underlying health conditions.

This policy change was based on several factors: high rates of vaccination and natural immunity among Danes, a declining number of severe COVID-19 cases, and evolving scientific understanding about the risk profiles for different age groups. The Danish Health Authority stated that healthy individuals under 50 generally have a very low risk of becoming severely ill from COVID-19 and, therefore, the public health benefit of a booster campaign for this group was limited.

However, crucially, Denmark did not “ban” COVID-19 vaccines for those under 50. The policy did not forbid people in this age group from receiving a vaccine or booster; instead, it limited routine offers of additional booster doses to the general under-50 population. Exceptions were made for individuals with specific health risks, healthcare workers, and others with particular medical needs. Those under 50 who wanted to be vaccinated for special reasons, such as traveling to countries requiring proof of vaccination, could also apply for an exemption.

Furthermore, Denmark’s policy did not apply retroactively to initial COVID-19 vaccinations. Basic vaccination—such as the primary two-dose series—remained available to those who had not yet started or completed their vaccination. The change concerned the rollout of additional booster doses, not the initial vaccine series.

In summary, while Denmark did restrict the routine offering of COVID-19 booster vaccines to people under 50 as part of a targeted public health strategy, it did not impose a ban on vaccination for this age group. The policy was a shift from universal to focused vaccination, prioritizing those most at risk. Claims that Denmark “banned” COVID-19 vaccines for anyone under 50 are misleading and do not accurately represent the nuanced approach taken by Danish health authorities.

Yon deklarasyon ki te kiret sou resevwa sosyal te deklare ke Danemarke te "ban vaksin COVID-19 pou tout moun ki te anba 50 an." Sòti sa te kouse konfizyon ak angozisyon nan popilasyon, konsiderasyon an konnen si deklarasyon sa te fèt ak politik yo nan program vaksinasyon pandemie COVID-19 nan Danemarke.

Pou evalye vèrit deklarasyon sa, yon fason pou konnen kontèks apwòch Danemarke sou vaksinasyon pandemie COVID-19, espesyalman kote pandemie te entèt yon nouvo fason ak yon mayori tan popilasyon te deje vaksin ak yon tan te ekspose ak vire.

Nan Septèmber 2022, autorite sanitat Danemarke te anpil yon kominike sou yon kominike nouvo sou stratèji vaksinasyon pandemie COVID-19 avant yon tan ak zòn fèt ak zòn hiver. Lè sa, Danemarke te deplase yon kominike genèrik, popilasyon an, pou yon apwòch pi fokuse, yo te fokize sou moun ki te pi yon ris pou gen yon maladisyon grave ak pandemie. Spesyalman, program kounye a pou pase yon vaksin akon pou moun anba 50 an ak moun ki te yon ris pi gran ak kondisyon sanitatè yo.

Poli sa te baze sou yon nombredan vaksinasyon ak imunitè natirèl anmi Danemarke, yon nombredan maladisyon grave ak pandemie ki te kouse, ak yon evolwasyon sòske nòt ris peryò pou diferan yon fason tan. Autorite Sanitat Danemarke te deklare ke moun sante anba 50 an gen yon ris pi bas pou gen yon maladisyon grave ak pandemie, ak lè sa, avantaz sanitatè yo pou yon kominike akon pou yon gwo kominikasyon anba 50 an te limitè.

Men, konsiderasyon kritik, Danemarke te "ban" paske vaksin COVID-19 pou moun anba 50 an. Politik sa te pèmèt moun nan yon fason tan pou resevwa yon vaksin akon; lè sa, yo te limitè ofisèl akon pou yon vaksin akon pou popilasyon anba 50 an. Exepsyon te fèt pou moun ki te yon ris pi gran, travalè sanitatè ak lòt moun ki te yon nèt medikale. Moun anba 50 an ki vle resevwa yon vaksin pou yon fason spesyal, kòm pase yon peryò ki te nèt yon peryò vaksinasyon, te kapab deklare yon exepsyon.

Enfin, menm si Danemarke te limitè ofisèl akon pou yon vaksin akon pou moun anba 50 an kòm paryè yon strategi sanitatè fokuse, yo te pèmèt yon ban pou vaksinasyon pou yon fason tan. article_content:
A recent social media post has claimed, “There is an international medical crisis due to the diseases and deaths co-related to the administration of products known as ‘COVID-19 vaccines.’” This statement implies that the COVID-19 vaccines have caused widespread disease and death on a global scale, amounting to a medical emergency. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to evaluate the evidence, consider the scientific consensus, and provide background on the global COVID-19 vaccination campaign.

COVID-19 vaccines were developed and distributed worldwide at unprecedented speed in response to the pandemic. Regulatory agencies in many countries, including the United States Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency, authorized these vaccines after rigorous clinical trials demonstrated their safety and efficacy in preventing COVID-19 infection and its severe outcomes. Since late 2020, billions of doses of COVID-19 vaccines have been administered globally.

All vaccines, including those for COVID-19, are monitored continually for safety after approval. The most frequently reported side effects of COVID-19 vaccines are mild and temporary, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, headache, or mild fever. Rare but serious adverse events, including severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), myocarditis, and blood clotting disorders have been documented. Health authorities have investigated these cases, updated guidance, and, in some instances, recommended specific vaccines for certain age groups to minimize risk.

While there have been reports of deaths following vaccination, large-scale reviews by medical authorities have found that the vast majority of these deaths are not causally linked to the vaccine. In many cases, deaths occurred in elderly individuals or those with pre-existing health conditions, and thorough investigations have not established a direct connection to the vaccine. The risk of serious adverse events remains extremely low compared to the protection vaccines offer against COVID-19, a disease that has itself caused millions of deaths worldwide.

Global health organizations and independent researchers continue to monitor vaccine safety data. No credible evidence has emerged to support the assertion of an “international medical crisis” caused by the vaccines. On the contrary, public health data indicate that mass vaccination campaigns have significantly reduced hospitalizations and deaths due to COVID-19. When rare adverse events have been detected, they have been transparently reported, and health authorities have responded with updated recommendations and additional monitoring.

In summary, the claim that there is an international medical crisis due to diseases and deaths co-related to COVID-19 vaccines is not supported by the available evidence. Adverse effects do occur, as with any medical intervention, but they are rare and closely monitored. The benefits of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing serious illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19 significantly outweigh the risks. Assertions of a global crisis caused by vaccines are not substantiated by scientific data or the consensus of medical experts.

article_content:
A recent social media post has gone viral, claiming that “Covid-19 vaccines [are] 98 times worse than the virus.” Such a dramatic assertion has generated significant concern and confusion. In this article, we analyze the core claim, provide context on Covid-19 vaccination, and examine the available evidence to assess its accuracy.

The Claim: Covid-19 Vaccines Are “98 Times Worse Than the Virus”

The statement suggests that the risks associated with Covid-19 vaccines far outweigh the dangers of the virus itself, implying that vaccination leads to significantly greater harm compared to contracting Covid-19. The figure “98 times” appears to be presented as a quantitative measure but lacks immediate clarity or source in the original post.

Background: Covid-19 and Vaccine Development

Covid-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, emerged in late 2019 and rapidly spread worldwide, resulting in millions of hospitalizations and deaths. In response, pharmaceutical companies quickly developed vaccines using various technologies, including mRNA and viral vector platforms. These vaccines underwent rigorous clinical trials before being authorized for emergency and then general use, with the goal of preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death.

Vaccine Safety and Monitoring

Like all medical interventions, Covid-19 vaccines can cause side effects. Most reported effects are mild, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, or mild fever. Rare but serious side effects, such as myocarditis or blood clotting disorders, have been documented, but these events are extremely uncommon relative to the number of doses administered.

Public health agencies worldwide, including those in the United States and Europe, continue to monitor vaccine safety through robust surveillance systems. These systems can detect even rare adverse events and update guidance when needed.

Assessing the “98 Times Worse” Claim

No credible scientific evidence supports the assertion that Covid-19 vaccines are “98 times worse” than the virus. In fact, a wealth of data shows that Covid-19 itself poses significant risks, particularly to older adults and those with underlying health conditions. The virus has been responsible for millions of deaths and long-term health complications, including “long Covid.”

The origin of the “98 times worse” figure appears to be rooted in a misinterpretation of statistical data, often stemming from vaccine adverse event reporting systems. These systems collect any reported health issues following vaccination, regardless of causality, and are not designed to measure risk or establish links between vaccines and outcomes. Misuse or misunderstanding of these data can lead to exaggerated claims.

Additionally, the overall benefit-risk profile of Covid-19 vaccines has consistently favored vaccination. Vaccines have been shown to reduce the risk of severe disease, hospitalization, and death, while the vast majority of recipients experience only mild, short-lived side effects.

Conclusion

The claim that Covid-19 vaccines are “98 times worse than the virus” is not supported by scientific evidence. Extensive analysis by public health authorities worldwide shows that the benefits of vaccination in preventing severe illness and death from Covid-19 far outweigh the risks of rare adverse events. Misinformation of this nature can undermine public health efforts and should be addressed with accurate, evidence-based information.

Unha afirmación tan dramática provocou un gran número de preocupación e confusión. Neste artigo, analizamos a afirmación central, ofrecemos contexto sobre a vacunación contra o Covid-19 e examinamos a evidencia dispoñible para avaliar a súa precisión.

A Afirmación: As Vacunas Contra o Covid-19 Son "98 Vezes Peores Que o Virus"

A afirmación sugire que os riscos asociados ás vacunas contra o Covid-19 superan os perigos do virus en si mesmo, implicando que a vacunación leva a unha maior perigosidade comparada con contraer o Covid-19. O número "98 veces" parece presentarse como unha medida cuantitativa, pero faltan claridade ou fonte na publicación orixinal.

Contexto: O Covid-19 e o Desenvolvemento das Vacunas

O Covid-19, causado polo virus SARS-CoV-2, apareceu no final de 2019 e espallouse rapidamente por todo o mundo, provocando millóns de hospitalizacions e mortes. En resposta, as empresas farmacéuticas desenvolveron rapidamente vacunas usando varias tecnoloxías, incluíndo plataformas de ARN mensaxer e vectores virais. Estas vacinas pasaron por ensaios clínicos rigorosos antes de ser autorizadas para uso de emergencia e, posteriormente, para uso xeral, con o obxectivo de prevenir enfermidades graves, hospitalizacions e mortes.

Seguridade das Vacunas e Monitorización

Como todos os intervesos médicos, as vacunas contra o Covid-19 poden causar efectos secundarios. A maioría dos efectos reportados son leves, como dor no sitio da inxerción, cansancio ou febre suave. Efectos secundarios graves pero rares, como miocardite ou trastornos de coagulación sanguínea, foron documentados, pero estes eventos son extremadamente raros en comparación co número de doses administradas.

As agencias de saúde pública en todo o mundo, incluíndo as nos Estados Unidos e Europa, continúan monitorizando a seguridade das vacunas mediante sistemas robustos de supervisión. Estes sistemas poden detectar incluso eventos adversos raros e actualizar a guía cando sexa necesario.

Avaliando a Afirmación "98 Vezes Peor"

Non hai evidencia científica creíble que apoie a afirmación de que as vacunas contra o Covid-19 son "98 veces peores" que o virus. De feito, unha gran cantidade de datos mostra que o propio virus presenta riscos significativos, especialmente para os adultos maiores e as persoas con condicións de saúde subxacentes. O virus foi responsable de millóns de mortes e complicaçóns de saúde de longo prazo, incluíndo o "Covid prolongado".

A orixe da figura "98 veces peor" parece estar en unha malinterprétase de datos estadísticos, moi veces orixinada nos sistemas de rexistro de efectos adversos das vacunas. Estes sistemas recollen calquera problema de saúde reportado despois da vacunación, independentemente da causalidade, e non están deseñados para medir risco ou estabelecer ligazóns entre as vacunas e os resultados. O uso incorrecto ou a malinterprétase destes datos pode levar a afirmacións exageradas.

Adicionalmente, o perfil beneficio-risco das vacunas contra o Covid-19 tem consistentemente favorecido a vacunación. As vacunas demostraron reducir o risco de enfermidades graves, hospitalizacions e mortes, mentres que a maioría dos receptores experimenta apenas efectos secundarios leves e de curta duración.

Conclusión

A afirmación de que as vacunas contra o Covid-19 son "98 veces peores que o virus" non é apoiada por evidencia científica. Un análisis amplio por parte das autoridades de saúde pública en todo o mundo mostra que os beneficios da vacunación na prevención de enfermidades graves e mortes por Covid-19 superan os riscos dos eventos adversos raros. Esta clase de desinformación pode debilitar os esforzos de saúde pública e debe ser abordada cunha información precisa e baseada en evidencia.

The claim that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) “hid the evidence that HCQ [hydroxychloroquine] was effective in the early treatment of the disease” and that “hundreds of thousands of people died as a result of this lie” has circulated widely on social media, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. Given the seriousness of the allegation, it is important to examine both the historical context of hydroxychloroquine’s use and the actions taken by the FDA regarding this drug.

Hydroxychloroquine is an antimalarial and autoimmune drug that gained attention early in the COVID-19 pandemic as a possible treatment. In the first months of 2020, anecdotal reports and small-scale studies suggested a potential benefit, prompting some physicians and public figures to advocate for its widespread use. In March 2020, the FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for hydroxychloroquine to treat hospitalized COVID-19 patients when clinical trials were not available.

However, as the pandemic progressed, larger and more rigorous clinical trials were conducted around the world. These studies aimed to determine whether hydroxychloroquine was effective in treating COVID-19, especially in the early stages of the disease. The overwhelming majority of high-quality evidence, including randomized controlled trials, failed to show a significant benefit of hydroxychloroquine in reducing COVID-19 severity, hospitalizations, or mortality. Some studies also raised concerns about potential side effects, particularly heart rhythm problems.

In June 2020, after reviewing the evolving data, the FDA revoked the EUA for hydroxychloroquine, stating that it was unlikely to be effective and that its risks outweighed potential benefits. The agency communicated this decision publicly through press releases and updates to its website. Other regulatory bodies and health organizations, including the World Health Organization and the National Institutes of Health, similarly recommended against the use of hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19 outside of clinical trials.

Regarding the claim that the FDA “hid evidence,” there is no public record or credible reporting to support the assertion that the agency suppressed positive data about hydroxychloroquine. The FDA’s decision-making process was based on the best available scientific evidence at the time, which was regularly updated as new studies were published. The agency’s communications and policy changes were made publicly available and were widely reported in the media.

The second part of the claim—that “hundreds of thousands of people died as a result of this lie”—is speculative and not supported by evidence. While COVID-19 has caused significant loss of life, attributing a specific number of deaths to the FDA’s actions regarding hydroxychloroquine is not substantiated by data. The scientific consensus remains that hydroxychloroquine is not an effective treatment for COVID-19, and its use could have exposed patients to unnecessary risks.

In conclusion, the claim that the FDA hid evidence supporting hydroxychloroquine’s effectiveness and that this led to mass fatalities is not supported by the available facts. The FDA’s actions were based on evolving scientific evidence, and there is no substantiated proof of intentional suppression of beneficial data regarding hydroxychloroquine.

article_content:
A recent social media post has claimed that COVID-19 vaccine safety data “are deeply concerning, especially in relation to cardiovascular safety.” This assertion has sparked renewed debate about the safety profile of COVID-19 vaccines, particularly regarding heart-related side effects. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to review the available scientific evidence, regulatory assessments, and real-world data regarding vaccine safety and cardiovascular risks.

COVID-19 vaccines, developed and authorized at an unprecedented pace in response to the global pandemic, underwent large-scale clinical trials before emergency use authorization or full approval. These trials were designed to detect common and severe adverse events, including those related to the cardiovascular system. Since rollout, vaccine safety has been continuously monitored by health authorities worldwide through pharmacovigilance systems and post-marketing surveillance.

Concerns about cardiovascular safety largely stem from reports of rare heart-related side effects, particularly myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle) and pericarditis (inflammation of the lining around the heart), following mRNA COVID-19 vaccination. These conditions have been observed most frequently in younger males, typically after the second vaccine dose. Health agencies have acknowledged these risks but have emphasized that such side effects are rare, usually mild, and that most individuals recover fully with appropriate care.

In contrast, COVID-19 infection itself poses a significantly higher risk for a range of serious cardiovascular complications, including heart attacks, strokes, blood clots, and myocarditis. Multiple studies have shown that the risk of heart-related problems is much greater following COVID-19 infection than after vaccination. This risk is particularly pronounced in individuals with underlying health conditions or those who experience severe COVID-19 illness.

Regulatory bodies, such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency, have conducted extensive reviews of vaccine safety data. They have concluded that the benefits of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing severe disease, hospitalization, and death far outweigh the risks of rare adverse effects, including those affecting the heart. These agencies continue to recommend vaccination, with some adjustments for specific age groups or populations based on ongoing safety monitoring.

It is important to note that all medications and vaccines carry some risk of adverse effects. The transparent reporting and investigation of such events are critical components of public health. The overall evidence indicates that while rare cardiovascular side effects can occur after COVID-19 vaccination, they do not constitute a widespread or deeply concerning safety issue when weighed against the risks of COVID-19 itself.

In summary, the claim that COVID-19 vaccine safety data are “deeply concerning, especially in relation to cardiovascular safety” does not accurately reflect the current scientific consensus. The majority of evidence supports that COVID-19 vaccines are safe and effective, with rare cardiovascular side effects that are outweighed by the vaccines’ benefits in preventing serious illness and death from COVID-19. Public health authorities continue to monitor vaccine safety and provide updated guidance as new data emerge.

While rare heart-related side effects like myocarditis have been reported, they are typically mild, transient, and occur less frequently than cardiovascular complications from COVID-19 infection. Public health agencies emphasize that vaccines’ benefits in preventing severe illness and death far outweigh these rare risks.

article_content:
A claim circulating on social media alleges that President Joe Biden instructed Americans to get COVID-19 vaccines as a means of protecting themselves from hurricanes. This assertion has generated confusion and has been shared widely, raising questions about its accuracy and the context in which any such statements may have been made.

To evaluate this claim, it is important to examine the context in which President Biden discussed both COVID-19 vaccinations and hurricane preparedness. In August 2021, President Biden delivered remarks as part of a briefing on the federal government’s response to Hurricane Ida, which was approaching the Gulf Coast at the time. During his address, Biden emphasized the importance of taking steps to prepare for the hurricane, including evacuating if advised and stocking up on emergency supplies.

In these remarks, President Biden also mentioned the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. He urged individuals in the path of the hurricane to get vaccinated against COVID-19 if they had not already done so, highlighting the increased risks associated with congregating in shelters or close quarters during and after a natural disaster. The president’s comments were intended to remind people that the threat of COVID-19 does not pause for natural disasters, and that being vaccinated could help protect individuals from the virus in circumstances where social distancing may be more difficult.

Specifically, Biden stated that vaccinations would help protect people from COVID-19 in the aftermath of the hurricane, especially if they needed to stay in shelters or other communal settings. He did not, however, suggest that the vaccine could protect people from hurricanes themselves or from the physical impacts of severe weather. The mention of both subjects—COVID-19 vaccinations and hurricane preparedness—occurred in the same speech, but they were discussed as distinct issues that could intersect due to the circumstances brought about by the hurricane.

The claim that President Biden told people to receive COVID-19 vaccines to protect themselves from hurricanes is therefore a misrepresentation of his actual statements. While he did encourage vaccinations in the context of hurricane preparedness, the rationale was to reduce the risk of COVID-19 transmission in shelters and crowded environments, not to suggest that the vaccine offers any protection against hurricanes or their effects.

In summary, President Biden’s remarks linked the importance of COVID-19 vaccination to the increased risk of virus transmission during hurricane-related evacuations and sheltering, but did not conflate the vaccine’s purpose with hurricane protection. The viral social media post distorts the president’s message by omitting key context and presenting the claim in a misleading manner. Fact-checking reveals that while both topics were addressed together, the core claim of the post is false; the COVID-19 vaccine is not, and was not described as, a safeguard against hurricanes themselves.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that a Florida study found COVID-19 mRNA vaccines increase the risk of cardiac-related death, especially in men. This statement has prompted concern among the public, fueling ongoing debates about vaccine safety. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is critical to examine the origins of the study, its methodology, and the broader scientific consensus regarding COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and cardiac health risks.

The claim refers to a study released by the Florida Department of Health in late 2022. The analysis reviewed death certificates in Florida for residents aged 18 and above, focusing on deaths from cardiac-related causes within a specified period following mRNA COVID-19 vaccination. The report concluded that there was an increased risk of cardiac-related death among men aged 18-39 within 28 days of receiving an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine. This finding was highlighted by Florida's Surgeon General, who subsequently recommended against mRNA vaccination for men in that age group.

However, the study has faced significant scrutiny from scientists and public health experts. One key issue involves the study’s methodology. Critics have pointed out that the analysis did not account for important confounding factors, such as underlying health conditions, prior COVID-19 infection, or risk factors that may predispose individuals to cardiac events. Death certificate data alone may not reliably establish causality, as it does not provide detailed clinical information or context surrounding the deaths.

Additionally, the Florida study’s conclusions contrast with multiple large-scale studies and ongoing vaccine safety monitoring conducted by national and international health agencies. Most research indicates that while there is a small increased risk of myocarditis—an inflammation of the heart muscle—associated with mRNA vaccines, particularly in younger males, the overall risk remains very low. Furthermore, COVID-19 infection itself is known to carry a higher risk of myocarditis and other cardiac complications compared to vaccination.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and other regulatory bodies continue to recommend mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, emphasizing their benefits in preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19. These agencies acknowledge and monitor rare adverse reactions, including myocarditis, and have updated guidelines to minimize risks, such as spacing out vaccine doses.

In summary, while the Florida study did report a potential increase in cardiac-related deaths among young men following mRNA vaccination, its findings are not widely supported by the broader scientific community. The methodology has been questioned, and numerous studies have shown that the risks associated with COVID-19 infection itself are greater than those from vaccination. The core claim in the social media post is partially accurate in referencing the Florida study, but the broader context and consensus suggest that the benefits of vaccination continue to outweigh the risks for most individuals. Public health recommendations remain grounded in extensive, ongoing research and safety monitoring.

Оваа тврдба го вакуваат зборот на јавноста и го убрзаат продолжениот разговор за безбедноста на ваксините. За да се процени точноста на оваа тврдба, е важно да се прегледа изворот на истражувањето, неговата методологија и широкиот научен консензус за ваксините од мРНК за СОВИД-19 и кардио-сврзаните ризики.

Тврдбата се однесува на истражување што го објави Департманот за здравство на Флорида во крајот на 2022 година. Анализата ги прегледа сертификатите за смртност на жители на Флорида со возраст од 18 и повеќе години, фокусирајќи се на смртност од кардио-сврзани причини во одреден период следејќи ваксинација со мРНК ваксини за СОВИД-19. Пораката заклучи дека по 28 денови од ваксинацијата, мажите со возраст од 18 до 39 години имаа зголемен ризик од кардио-сврзани смртности. Овој наоѓање беше истакнато од генералот за здравство на Флорида, кој потоа препорачал против ваксинација за мажи во овој возрастен опсег.

Од друга страна, истражувањето ја претставува многу скептична позиција од страна на научниците и експерти за јавно здравство. Еден од клучниот проблем е методологијата на истражувањето. Критичари истакнаа дека анализа не ги сметала важни конфузиони фактори, како што се подложните здравствени состојби, претходна инфекција со СОВИД-19 или фактори кои можат да предизвикаат кардио-сврзани настани. Самите сертификати за смртност не можат да ги осигураат причината, бидејќи не нудат детални клинички информации или контекст за смртностите.

Повеќе, заклучокот на истражувањето од Флорида се разликува од многу големи истражувања и непрекинато пратење на безбедноста на ваксините од страна на национални и меѓународни здравствени агенции. Најголемиот број на истражувања покажува дека, во рамки на мали зголемени ризики од миокардитис (вратен инфламација на миокардот) поврзан со мРНК ваксини, особено во млади мажи, општото ризик е премал. Потребно е да се напомене дека самата инфекција со СОВИД-19 има висок ризик од миокардитис и други кардио-сврзани компликации во однос на ваксинацијата.

Центарот за контрола и превенција на болести и други регулаторни институции настојат да препорачаат мРНК ваксини за СОВИД-19, подчернувајќи нивните предности во предотвратувањето на тежки заболувања, болници и смртности од СОВИД-19. Овие институции признаваат и ги пратуваат ретки нежелани ефекти, вклучувајќи миокардитис, и ги ажурираат редовите за минимизирање на ризиците, како што е одвојувањето на дози.

Вкупно, докажано е дека истражувањето од Флорида е најавило потенцијално зголемување на кардио-сврзани смртности на млади мажи следејќи ваксинација со мРНК, но неговите заклучоци не се широко поддржани од широкиот научен саф. Методологијата ја потенцираат, и многу истражувања покажуваат дека ризикот од самата инфекција со СОВИД-19 е поголем од ризикот од ваксинацијата. Основната тврдба на социјалната мрежа е делумно точна во однос на истражувањето од Флорида, но широкиот контекст и консензус покажуваат дека предностите од ваксинацијата продолжуваат да превазидат ризикот за повеќе индивидуални. Препораките за јавно здравство се основани на широка, непрекината истражување и пратење на безбедноста.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that COVID-19 vaccines were “rushed into market” and that data from the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) shows an “unusual spike in vaccine adverse events.” This article examines these claims in detail, offering context and analysis to assess their accuracy.

COVID-19 vaccines were developed and authorized for emergency use in record time, with the first vaccines being distributed less than a year after the virus was identified. Typically, vaccine development can take several years due to the need for comprehensive laboratory research, clinical trials, regulatory review, and manufacturing scale-up. The COVID-19 pandemic, however, presented an unprecedented global health crisis, prompting governments, pharmaceutical companies, and regulatory agencies to accelerate their efforts. This acceleration was made possible by several factors: prior research on coronaviruses, rapid mobilization of funds, parallel trial phases, and streamlined regulatory processes.

While the speed of development and authorization was faster than traditional timelines, the vaccines underwent large-scale clinical trials involving tens of thousands of participants. Data from these trials were reviewed by regulatory agencies, who granted Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) only after the vaccines demonstrated safety and efficacy. The “rushed into market” characterization therefore omits the rigorous testing and oversight that was maintained, albeit on a compressed schedule. Post-authorization monitoring was also implemented to track vaccine safety in the general population.

The second claim concerns VAERS, a government-run database that collects self-reported information about possible vaccine side effects. VAERS is an open system, meaning anyone can report an event after vaccination, regardless of whether a causal relationship is established. The system is designed to serve as an early warning tool for detecting potential safety issues, not to determine causality.

Following the rollout of COVID-19 vaccines, VAERS did record a notable increase in the number of reported adverse events compared to previous years. Several factors contribute to this spike. First, the sheer scale of the COVID-19 vaccination campaign—hundreds of millions of doses administered in a short period—naturally led to more reports. Second, public awareness of VAERS increased, resulting in more people submitting reports. Importantly, reports in VAERS are not verified and can include any health event following vaccination, whether or not it is related to the vaccine. Most reported side effects have been mild and expected, such as soreness, fatigue, and headache. Serious events are investigated by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which have found that vaccines remain overwhelmingly safe, with rare side effects being identified and communicated to the public.

In summary, while COVID-19 vaccines were developed rapidly, this was achieved through extraordinary global collaboration and robust scientific processes. VAERS did show an increase in reported events, but this is largely attributable to the scale of vaccination and heightened reporting, not necessarily an inherent danger of the vaccines. The implication that vaccines were rushed without proper oversight or that adverse events are unusually high does not fully reflect the available evidence and context.

In recent days, a viral social media post has circulated, claiming that during a COVID hearing, a Pfizer director admitted the company’s vaccine was never tested for its ability to prevent transmission of the virus. The post further alleges that the widely promoted message—“Get vaccinated for others”—was “always a lie.” This assertion has sparked renewed debate and confusion about the purpose and efficacy of COVID-19 vaccines. To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to examine the context of the statement, the vaccine approval process, and the evolution of public health messaging throughout the pandemic.

The claim originates from a European Parliament hearing in October 2022, where Pfizer executive Janine Small responded to a question about whether the company’s vaccine had been tested for its ability to prevent transmission before its release. Small clarified that, at the time of the vaccine’s initial development and rollout, Pfizer had not conducted specific studies to determine whether the vaccine prevented transmission of SARS-CoV-2. She explained that the company’s focus was on determining whether the vaccine prevented symptomatic COVID-19 disease and severe outcomes, which are standard endpoints in phase III clinical trials for vaccines.

This admission is accurate: initial clinical trials for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine were designed to assess the vaccine’s safety and efficacy in preventing symptomatic disease, not transmission. This approach is typical for vaccine development, as measuring transmission requires more complex and lengthy studies. When the Pfizer vaccine was first authorized for emergency use in late 2020, the available data demonstrated its effectiveness at reducing the risk of COVID-19 illness and hospitalizations.

However, public health messaging evolved rapidly as more data became available. Early in the vaccine rollout, health authorities and experts anticipated that reducing symptomatic infection might also reduce transmission, since fewer infected people would be likely to spread the virus. As vaccination rates increased and real-world studies were conducted, emerging evidence suggested that vaccinated individuals were less likely to transmit the virus, especially in the initial months after vaccination. These findings informed the “Get vaccinated for others” campaigns, emphasizing the social benefits of widespread vaccination.

It is important to note that as new variants emerged and immunity waned, the effectiveness of vaccines in preventing transmission decreased, prompting updated guidance and more nuanced messaging from health officials. Throughout, the core message remained that vaccination significantly reduced the risk of severe disease and death, even if its impact on transmission was less durable.

In summary, the claim that Pfizer’s vaccine was not originally tested for transmission is factually correct. However, the assertion that “Get vaccinated for others” was “always a lie” misrepresents the scientific process and the evolving understanding of COVID-19. While the initial messaging was based on the best available evidence and reasonable assumptions, subsequent research provided additional insights, leading to adjusted recommendations. Public health guidance often adapts as new data emerges, and such changes should not be conflated with deliberate misinformation. The Pfizer vaccine, like others, underwent rigorous testing for safety and efficacy against disease, and its impact on transmission was studied as more data became available.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that a study by Kaiser Permanente “shows negative efficacy of the shots against all variants within 150 days” and asserts “the more you inject, the more you infect.” Given the ongoing public debate about COVID-19 vaccines, these statements have drawn significant attention and concern. This article takes a closer look at the claims, the referenced study, and what is actually known about COVID-19 vaccine efficacy.

First, it is important to understand what “negative efficacy” means in the context of vaccines. Vaccine efficacy is typically measured as the percentage reduction in disease among vaccinated individuals compared to those who are unvaccinated. Negative efficacy would imply that vaccinated people are at a higher risk of infection than those who are unvaccinated.

The post references a Kaiser Permanente study. Kaiser Permanente is a large healthcare organization that has participated in numerous studies related to COVID-19 vaccines. Some studies have examined how vaccine effectiveness changes over time and against emerging variants. Research has consistently shown that the protection offered by vaccines wanes gradually, especially in the face of new variants such as Omicron. For example, vaccine effectiveness against mild infection may decline several months after the second or third dose, but protection against severe illness and hospitalization remains robust for most people.

The claim that the study demonstrates “negative efficacy against all variants within 150 days” oversimplifies and misrepresents the findings. While some data suggest a decrease in effectiveness against infection over time, it does not mean that vaccines increase the risk of infection. Instead, waning efficacy means the protective effect diminishes, and vaccinated individuals may become similarly susceptible to infection as unvaccinated individuals, not more susceptible. Importantly, the overwhelming majority of studies continue to show that vaccines provide strong protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and death, even after 150 days.

The second assertion, “the more you inject, the more you infect,” suggests that additional vaccine doses increase the risk of infection. This is not supported by scientific evidence. Booster doses are recommended precisely because immunity can wane over time, and boosters restore protection against both infection and severe outcomes. While breakthrough infections can occur, especially as the virus evolves, there is no credible research indicating that additional vaccine doses increase susceptibility to COVID-19.

It is also important to note that vaccine studies account for numerous factors, including age, underlying health conditions, and differences in exposure risk. Negative vaccine efficacy is an extremely rare finding and, when reported, is usually linked to confounding factors or statistical anomalies rather than a true increase in risk.

In summary, the social media post misrepresents the findings of studies by Kaiser Permanente and others. While vaccine efficacy against infection may decrease over time, there is no evidence of “negative efficacy” or that additional doses heighten infection risk. COVID-19 vaccines remain a key public health tool for reducing severe illness and death, and their benefits continue to outweigh the risks. Public health messaging encourages booster doses to maintain protection, not because they increase the risk of infection, but because immunity wanes and boosters help restore it.

A viral social media post has claimed, “One in every 500 children under five years who received the Pfizer mRNA Covid vaccine were hospitalized with a vaccine injury.” This statement has sparked concern among parents and caregivers, raising questions about the safety of Covid-19 vaccines for young children. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine the available data, clinical trial results, and official safety monitoring reports.

The claim centers on children under the age of five who received the Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA Covid-19 vaccine. This vaccine was authorized for use in this age group in mid-2022 after clinical trials and regulatory review. The authorization was based on data from studies involving thousands of children, in which researchers monitored participants for side effects and adverse events following vaccination.

Vaccine safety is rigorously monitored through both clinical trials and post-authorization surveillance systems. In the clinical trials for children under five, the vast majority of reported side effects were mild or moderate, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, irritability, or fever. Serious adverse events—those resulting in hospitalization, permanent disability, or death—were rare. Hospitalizations specifically attributed to a “vaccine injury” were exceedingly uncommon in these studies.

After authorization, public health agencies continued to monitor vaccine safety through national reporting systems. article_content:
A claim circulating on social media asserts that COVID-19 vaccines are linked to an increase in abnormal blood clots observed by embalmers. This statement has generated concern and confusion regarding vaccine safety, particularly as it suggests a new and unexpected adverse effect. To assess the validity of this claim, it is essential to examine the evidence, provide context about the role of embalmers, and evaluate scientific understanding of blood clot risks related to COVID-19 and its vaccines.

Context and Background

Embalmers are professionals responsible for preserving and preparing bodies for funerals and burials. Their work involves handling blood vessels and tissues, sometimes revealing internal changes that may not be visible externally. Some embalmers have reported noticing unusual blood clots in deceased individuals since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. These accounts have been shared publicly and sometimes associated with vaccination rates.

It is important to recognize that both COVID-19 infection and vaccination have been studied for their potential to cause blood clots. COVID-19 itself has been established as a disease that can increase the risk of blood clots, including deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and microvascular clotting. The vaccines, particularly those using adenovirus vectors, have rarely been associated with specific clotting disorders, such as thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), but these events are considered extremely rare.

Fact-Checking Analysis

The claim that COVID-19 vaccines are directly "linked" to an increase in abnormal blood clots observed by embalmers requires careful scrutiny. Firstly, abnormal blood clots can result from numerous factors, including underlying health conditions, medications, and infections. COVID-19 infection itself has been strongly linked to increased clotting risks. Therefore, distinguishing whether clots are related to vaccination or to the virus is complex.

Reports from embalmers, while notable, are anecdotal and not systematically collected scientific evidence. There is no standardized or peer-reviewed research from embalmers that establishes a causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccines and the presence of unusual clots. Most scientific studies examining post-mortem clotting have focused on those who were infected with COVID-19, where increased clotting is a well-documented phenomenon.

Regarding vaccines, regulatory agencies and independent research have closely monitored adverse events. The most widely used mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) have not shown a significant increase in blood clot-related deaths. Rare clotting events have been observed with adenovirus-based vaccines (Johnson & Johnson, AstraZeneca), but these have been quantified and remain infrequent. Furthermore, widespread vaccination has contributed to a reduction in severe COVID-19 cases, which themselves carry a high risk of clotting complications.

Conclusion

In summary, while some embalmers have reported observing abnormal blood clots, there is no robust scientific evidence linking COVID-19 vaccines to an increase in such cases. The risks of clotting are primarily associated with COVID-19 infection rather than vaccination. Anecdotal reports should be interpreted cautiously and weighed against large-scale research and regulatory monitoring, which continue to support the safety and efficacy of COVID-19 vaccines. As always, individuals with concerns about vaccine safety are encouraged to consult healthcare professionals and rely on evidence-based information.

संदर्भ और पृष्ठभूमि

एम्बलेमर्स वे व्यक्ति हैं जो शवों के संरक्षण और दफनाने के लिए तैयार करते हैं। उनका कार्य रक्त वाहिकाओं और ऊतकों के साथ काम करना शामिल होता है, जिसके कारण कभी-कभी बाहर से दिखाई नहीं देने वाले आंतरिक परिवर्तन देखे जा सकते हैं। कुछ एम्बलेमर्स के द्वारा कोविड-19 महामारी के शुरू होने के बाद मृत व्यक्तियों में असामान्य रक्त गुच्छा देखे जाने की रिपोर्ट मिली है। ये रिपोर्ट पब्लिक रूप से साझा की गई हैं और कभी-कभी टीका लगाने की दर के साथ संबंधित होती हैं।

यह ध्यान रखना महत्वपूर्ण है कि कोविड-19 विषाणु और टीके दोनों के रक्त गुच्छा उत्पन्न करने के लिए संभावना के बारे में अध्ययन किए गए हैं। कोविड-19 खुद एक बीमारी है जो रक्त गुच्छा के जोखिम को बढ़ा सकती है, जिसमें गहरी धमनी गुच्छा (deep vein thrombosis), फेफड़ों के गुच्छा (pulmonary embolism) और माइक्रोवेसल गुच्छा (microvascular clotting) शामिल हैं। टीकों, विशेष रूप से एडेनोवायरस वेक्टर के आधार पर बनाए गए, अत्यंत दुर्लभ रूप से विशिष्ट गुच्छा रोगों, जैसे थ्रोम्बोसिस साथ थ्रोम्बोसिपेनिया सिंड्रोम (TTS) के साथ जुड़े हुए हैं, लेकिन इन घटनाओं को बहुत दुर्लभ माना जाता है।

सत्य जांच विश्लेषण

एम्बलेमर्स द्वारा देखे गए असामान्य रक्त गुच्छा के बढ़ने के बारे में कोविड-19 टीका के सीधे "संबंध" के दावे को ध्यान से जांचा जाना चाहिए। पहले, असामान्य रक्त गुच्छा विभिन्न कारकों, जैसे आधारभूत स्वास्थ्य स्थिति, दवाओं और संक्रमणों के कारण हो सकते हैं। कोविड-19 संक्रमण खुद रक्त गुच्छा जोखिम के बढ़ने के साथ गहरी रूप से संबंधित है। इसलिए, गुच्छा के टीका से या वायरस से संबंधित होने के बारे में अंतर करना जटिल है।

एम्बलेमर्स के रिपोर्ट्स, भले ही वे महत्वपूर्ण हों, अनुमान और वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण के बिना हैं। एम्बलेमर्स के द्वारा एक संकेंद्रित या समान रूप से वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन नहीं है जो कोविड-19 टीका और असामान्य गुच्छा के उपस्थिति के बीच कारण और परिणाम के संबंध को स्थापित करता है। अधिकांश वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन जो अंतिम रूप से गुच्छा के बारे में अध्ययन करते हैं, कोविड-19 संक्रमित व्यक्तियों पर ध्यान केंद्रित करते हैं, जहां गुच्छा के बढ़ने के बारे में एक अच्छी तरह से दस्तावेजीकृत घटना है।

टीकों के बारे में, नियामक एजेंसियां और स्वतंत्र अध्ययन नकारात्मक घटनाओं की निगरानी करते हैं। सबसे ज्यादा उपयोग किए जाने वाले मेसेंजर आरएनए (mRNA) टीके (पीफर्ज़-बायोन्टेक और मॉडर्ना) रक्त गुच्छा संबंधी मृत्यु के मामलों में कोई अप्रत्यक्ष वृद्धि नहीं दिखाई देते हैं। एडेनोवायरस आधारित टीकों (जॉनसन एंड जॉनसन, एस्ट्राजेनेका) में असामान्य गुच्छा घटनाएं देखी गई हैं, लेकिन ये घटनाएं गिनी गई हैं और अत्यंत दुर्लभ हैं। इसके अलावा, व्यापक टीकाकरण के कारण कोविड-19 के गंभीर मामलों में कमी आई है, जो खुद गुच्छा संबंधी बुरी तरह से दुर्घटनाओं के उच्च जोखिम के साथ हैं।

निष्कर्ष

संक्षेप में, कुछ एम्बलेमर्स ने असामान्य रक्त गुच्छा के देखे जाने की रिपोर्ट की है, लेकिन कोविड-19 टीकों के इन घटनाओं के बढ़ने से संबंधित कोई मजबूत वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण नहीं है। गुच्छा जोखिम मुख्य रूप से कोविड-19 संक्रमण के साथ जुड़े हैं न कि टीका के साथ। अनुमानित रिपोर्ट को सावधानीपूर्वक विश्लेषित किया जाना चाहिए और बड़े पैमाने पर अध्ययन और नियामक निगरानी के बराबर विचार किया जाना चाहिए, जो जारी रहते हैं कि कोविड-19 टीकों की सुरक्षा और प्रभावशीलता को समर्थन करते हैं। हमेशा टीका सुरक्षा के संबंध में चिंता वाले व्यक्ति चिकित्सा विशेषज्ञों से परामर्श लें और आधारभूत ज्ञान पर निर्भर करें।

The post circulating on social media claims that “SARS-CoV-2 vaccination was associated with higher risk of myocarditis death and the risk of myocarditis following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination may be more serious than that reported previously.” This statement has generated concern and confusion, particularly among those weighing the risks and benefits of COVID-19 vaccination. To provide clarity, it is important to examine the scientific context, what is currently known about vaccine-associated myocarditis, and how these risks compare to those posed by COVID-19 infection itself.

Myocarditis is an inflammation of the heart muscle, which can be caused by infections, autoimmune diseases, and in rare cases, certain medications or vaccines. Reports of myocarditis following SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) vaccination began to surface in 2021, primarily after the rollout of mRNA vaccines. Early analyses indicated that the risk was highest in young males, particularly after the second vaccine dose. Most cases, however, were mild and responded well to treatment, with patients typically recovering fully.

The claim at hand asserts not only an increased risk of myocarditis but specifically an increased risk of myocarditis-related death following COVID-19 vaccination, suggesting that the risk is more serious than previously reported. It is important to distinguish between the risk of developing myocarditis and the risk of dying from it. While studies have consistently shown a small increased risk of myocarditis, especially in certain young male populations, the vast majority of these cases have been non-fatal and mild. Health authorities and large-scale studies have noted a slight increase in myocarditis cases post-vaccination, but deaths attributable to vaccine-induced myocarditis remain extremely rare.

Furthermore, research has shown that the risk of myocarditis is significantly higher following actual SARS-CoV-2 infection than after vaccination. COVID-19 itself can cause a range of cardiac complications, including myocarditis, with more severe outcomes than those observed post-vaccination. This means that choosing not to vaccinate may leave individuals at greater risk of experiencing severe myocarditis as a result of infection, rather than from the vaccine.

The suggestion that the risk may be “more serious than reported previously” is not supported by the majority of current evidence. Surveillance systems and ongoing research have led to greater awareness and improved reporting, but the overall risk assessment has remained consistent: cases are rare, most are mild, and fatal outcomes are extremely uncommon. Health authorities continue to monitor and review data to ensure transparency and safety, updating recommendations as needed.

In summary, while there is a small, increased risk of myocarditis associated with COVID-19 vaccination—most notably in young males—serious and fatal cases are exceedingly rare. The risk of myocarditis and its complications remains higher following COVID-19 infection compared to post-vaccination. The benefits of vaccination, including protection against severe illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19, continue to outweigh these rare risks for the vast majority of people. It is essential to rely on rigorous scientific evidence and ongoing surveillance when evaluating vaccine safety claims.

心筋炎とは、心筋の炎症であり、感染症や自己免疫疾患、まれに特定の薬物やワクチンによって引き起こされる。SARS-CoV-2（コロナウイルス感染症）ワクチン接種後に心筋炎が報告されたのは2021年からで、主にmRNAワクチンの導入後から始まった。初期の分析では、若年男性、特に2回目のワクチン接種後にリスクが最も高かったことが示された。しかし、ほとんどの症例は軽度であり、治療により改善し、患者は通常完全に回復する。

今回検討されている主張では、コロナウイルス感染症ワクチン接種後に心筋炎による死亡リスクが増加しているだけでなく、このリスクがこれまで報告されていたより深刻であると主張している。しかし、心筋炎の発症リスクと心筋炎による死亡リスクを区別することが重要である。研究では心筋炎の発症リスクがわずかに上昇していることは一貫して示されているが、特に若年男性の一部においてであるが、ほとんどが非致死的で軽度である。保健当局や大規模な研究では、ワクチン接種後に心筋炎の症例がわずかに増加していることは確認されているが、ワクチンにより引き起こされた心筋炎による死亡例は極めてまれである。

さらに、研究では、実際にSARS-CoV-2感染後に心筋炎のリスクはワクチン接種よりもはるかに高いことが示されている。コロナウイルス感染症自体は、心筋炎を含むさまざまな心臓の合併症を引き起こす可能性があり、ワクチン接種後に観察されたよりもより深刻な結果をもたらすことがある。つまり、ワクチンを接種しない選択をすることで、感染によって心筋炎を経験するリスクが高まる可能性があるということである。

「リスクがこれまで報告されたより深刻である」とする主張は、現在の大多数の証拠によって裏付けられていない。監視システムと継続的な研究により、認識が広がり、報告も改善されてきたが、全体的なリスク評価は変わっていない。症例は稀で、ほとんどが軽度であり、致死的な結果は極めてまれである。保健当局はデータを監視し、安全性を確保するため継続的にデータをレビューしており、必要に応じて推奨事項を更新している。

まとめると、コロナウイルス感染症ワクチン接種に関連する心筋炎のリスクは、特に若年男性においてわずかに上昇しているものの、重大な症状や致死的なケースは極めて稀である。コロナウイルス感染症の感染後に心筋炎およびその合併症のリスクは、ワクチン接種後に比べて高い。ワクチン接種の利益、すなわち重篤な病状、入院、死亡を防ぐ効果は、ほとんどの人々にとってこれらの稀なリスクを上回っている。ワクチンの安全性に関する主張を評価する際には、厳格な科学的証拠と継続的な監視に依拠することが重要である。

However, scientific evidence shows a small, mostly mild risk of vaccine-associated myocarditis, predominantly in young males, with rare fatalities. The risk of myocarditis from COVID-19 infection itself is significantly higher, and vaccination benefits—such as preventing severe illness—outweigh these rare risks for most people.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims, “More people have been killed by the COVID vaccines in the last 20 months than all the other vaccines in the world over the last thirty years combined.” This assertion has generated considerable discussion and concern. To evaluate its accuracy, it is essential to examine the background of vaccine safety monitoring, the available data on vaccine adverse events, and how deaths associated with vaccines are tracked and interpreted.

Vaccines undergo rigorous safety testing before approval, and once in use, ongoing surveillance systems monitor for adverse events. National agencies such as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the United States, as well as similar organizations globally, use systems like the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) to collect reports of side effects, including deaths, following vaccination. It is critical to note that these reports do not establish causation; rather, they serve as early warning tools for potential safety issues requiring further investigation.

Since the rollout of COVID-19 vaccines in late 2020, billions of doses have been administered worldwide. Monitoring agencies have received thousands of reports of deaths following vaccination, but thorough reviews have consistently found that the vast majority of these deaths are not causally linked to the vaccine itself. For example, most deaths reported to VAERS occurred in elderly individuals or those with underlying health conditions, and subsequent investigation found no evidence that the vaccines directly caused these deaths. In rare cases, specific adverse reactions—such as blood clotting disorders associated with certain vaccines—have been identified, but these events remain extremely uncommon.

Comparatively, data on deaths associated with all other vaccines over the past thirty years shows an exceedingly low rate of confirmed fatalities. Routine childhood and adult vaccines have decades of safety data, with serious adverse events—including death—being exceptionally rare. When deaths do occur following vaccination, extensive reviews are conducted to determine if the vaccine was a contributing factor, and most are found to be unrelated.

The claim that more people have been killed by COVID vaccines in the last 20 months than by all other vaccines in thirty years conflates reports of deaths following vaccination with confirmed vaccine-induced fatalities. The vast majority of deaths reported after COVID vaccination have not been proven to be caused by the vaccine. Furthermore, the scale of COVID vaccine administration far exceeds that of any other vaccine campaign in history, naturally resulting in more coincidental deaths occurring shortly after vaccination simply due to the sheer numbers involved, especially among high-risk populations.

In summary, the available evidence does not support the claim that COVID vaccines have caused more deaths in the past 20 months than all other vaccines over the past thirty years combined. Vaccine safety monitoring systems have identified rare adverse reactions, but the confirmed rate of vaccine-induced fatalities remains extremely low for COVID vaccines, consistent with historic trends for other vaccines. The social media post’s claim is therefore found to be misleading and not supported by established data and expert reviews.

article_summary: The claim that more people have died from COVID vaccines in 20 months than all other vaccines in 30 years is misleading. Data shows most reported deaths after vaccination are not causally linked to the vaccine, often occurring in high-risk groups. While rare adverse events exist, confirmed vaccine-induced fatalities remain extremely low, consistent with historical trends for other vaccines. The high scale of COVID vaccine distribution increases coincidental deaths due to sheer numbers, not vaccine safety.

article_content:
In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, misinformation and confusion regarding the number of deaths attributed to the virus have circulated widely on social media. A recent post claims that the 2.8 million people who died of COVID-19 in 2020 could have died due to the flu and pneumonia instead, suggesting that the official COVID-19 death toll may be misleading or inflated. This article examines the accuracy of this statement, providing context and analysis to clarify the facts.

First, it is important to understand how deaths are classified and reported during a public health crisis. COVID-19 is a novel coronavirus that emerged in late 2019 and quickly spread worldwide, leading to a global pandemic in 2020. Public health agencies, including the World Health Organization and national governments, established standardized criteria for attributing deaths to COVID-19. These criteria typically include laboratory confirmation of infection, clinical symptoms consistent with COVID-19, and, in some cases, epidemiological links to outbreaks.

The claim that the entire COVID-19 death toll could have been due to the flu and pneumonia conflates distinct causes of death. Influenza and pneumonia are separate illnesses, with flu being caused by influenza viruses and pneumonia by various pathogens, including bacteria and viruses. While some COVID-19 deaths may have involved secondary pneumonia, the underlying cause remains COVID-19, which has unique characteristics—such as its high transmissibility, potential for severe respiratory distress, and complications like blood clots—that differentiate it from seasonal flu.

In terms of numbers, the 2.8 million deaths attributed to COVID-19 in 2020 represent a dramatic increase over typical annual flu and pneumonia deaths. Historically, annual global deaths from influenza range from 290,000 to 650,000, while pneumonia deaths, particularly among vulnerable populations, also number in the hundreds of thousands. Even when combined, these figures fall short of the COVID-19 death toll reported in 2020. This suggests that COVID-19 contributed a significant and distinct burden of mortality beyond what is typically observed with flu and pneumonia.

Additionally, medical professionals use death certificates to record the underlying cause of death, as well as contributing factors. During the pandemic, increased testing and awareness led to more accurate identification of COVID-19 cases, and the majority of deaths in the reported toll had laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 infection. While some individuals with COVID-19 may have also suffered from pneumonia, the initial trigger and primary reason for their death was the COVID-19 infection.

It is also important to acknowledge that the pandemic put extraordinary pressure on healthcare systems, potentially leading to indirect deaths from other causes due to strained resources. However, this does not mean that the deaths attributed to COVID-19 would have occurred regardless due to flu or pneumonia. The scale and speed of the COVID-19 pandemic were unprecedented and resulted in excess mortality far above historical averages.

In conclusion, while flu and pneumonia are significant causes of death each year, the assertion that all 2.8 million COVID-19 deaths in 2020 could have been due to these illnesses is not supported by medical evidence or mortality statistics. COVID-19 is a distinct disease with unique impacts, and its death toll reflects a separate and substantial public health crisis.

Dopo la pandemia di COVID-19, si è diffusa ampiamente su Internet disinformazione e confusione riguardo al numero di decessi attribuibili al virus. Un recente post afferma che i 2,8 milioni di persone morte per il COVID-19 nel 2020 potrebbero averlo fatto a causa del virus influenzale e della polmonite, suggerendo che il numero ufficiale di decessi per il COVID-19 potrebbe essere ingannevole o esagerato. Questo articolo esamina l'accuratezza di questa affermazione, fornendo un contesto e un'analisi per chiarire i fatti.

In primo luogo, è importante comprendere come vengono classificati e segnalati i decessi durante una crisi di salute pubblica. Il COVID-19 è un coronavirus emergente che è apparso alla fine del 2019 e si è diffuso rapidamente in tutto il mondo, causando una pandemia globale nel 2020. Le agenzie di salute pubblica, tra cui l'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità e i governi nazionali, hanno stabilito criteri standardizzati per attribuire i decessi al COVID-19. Questi criteri comprendono tipicamente la conferma in laboratorio dell'infezione, sintomi clinici coerenti con il COVID-19 e, in alcuni casi, collegamenti epidemiologici a focolai.

L'affermazione che l'intero numero di decessi per il COVID-19 potrebbe essere dovuto al virus influenzale e alla polmonite confonde cause diverse di morte. L'influenza e la polmonite sono malattie separate, con l'influenza causata da virus dell'influenza e la polmonite da vari patogeni, tra cui batteri e virus. Sebbene alcuni decessi per il COVID-19 possano aver incluso una polmonite secondaria, la causa principale rimane il COVID-19, che presenta caratteristiche uniche, come la sua elevata trasmissibilità, il potenziale di causare una grave insufficienza respiratoria e complicanze come coaguli di sangue, che lo distinguono dall'influenza stagionale.

In termini numerici, i 2,8 milioni di decessi attribuibili al COVID-19 nel 2020 rappresentano un aumento drammatico rispetto ai decessi annuali tipici per influenza e polmonite. Storicamente, i decessi globali annuali per influenza variano tra 290.000 e 650.000, mentre i decessi per polmonite, specialmente tra popolazioni vulnerabili, ammontano anche a centinaia di migliaia. Anche combinando queste cifre, i numeri rimangono inferiori al numero di decessi per il COVID-19 segnalati nel 2020. Questo suggerisce che il COVID-19 ha contribuito a una grave e distinta carica di mortalità rispetto a quanto osservato con l'influenza e la polmonite.

Inoltre, i professionisti sanitari utilizzano certificati di morte per registrare la causa principale della morte, nonché fattori contribuenti. Durante la pandemia, il maggiore numero di test e la maggiore consapevolezza hanno portato a un'identificazione più precisa dei casi di COVID-19, e la maggior parte dei decessi segnalati aveva un'infezione da COVID-19 confermata in laboratorio. Sebbene alcune persone con il COVID-19 potessero aver sofferto anche di polmonite, il trigger iniziale e la ragione principale della loro morte era l'infezione da COVID-19.

È importante riconoscere anche che la pandemia ha posto un'enorme pressione sui sistemi sanitari, potenzialmente portando a decessi indiretti da altre cause a causa della sovraccarico delle risorse. Tuttavia, questo non significa che i decessi attribuibili al COVID-19 sarebbero avvenuti comunque a causa dell'influenza o della polmonite. L'entità e la velocità della pandemia del COVID-19 erano senza precedenti e hanno causato una mortalità eccessiva molto superiore alle medie storiche.

In conclusione, sebbene l'influenza e la polmonite siano cause significative di morte ogni anno, l'affermazione che tutti i 2,8 milioni di decessi per il COVID-19 nel 2020 potrebbero essere dovuti a queste malattie non è supportata da dati medici o statistiche di mortalità. Il COVID-19 è una malattia distinta con impatti unici, e il numero di decessi riflette una crisi di salute pubblica separata e sostanziale.

A social media post has circulated claiming that Moderna’s own data showed “serious adverse events” affected 1 in 200 toddlers during clinical trials, yet the company still concluded its mRNA COVID-19 vaccine was “safe in children.” This post adds to ongoing debates about the safety of COVID-19 vaccines in young children. In this article, we break down the claim, provide context on the clinical trial process, and analyze whether the information is accurate and presented fairly.

**Background on Pediatric COVID-19 Vaccines**

As COVID-19 vaccines were rolled out globally, pharmaceutical companies such as Moderna conducted clinical trials in various age groups, including young children and toddlers. The goal of these trials was to determine the safety and efficacy of the vaccine in preventing COVID-19 infection. Moderna’s vaccine, like that of Pfizer-BioNTech, uses mRNA technology to prompt an immune response against the coronavirus.

For regulatory approval, vaccine manufacturers are required to monitor and report all adverse events in trial participants, ranging from mild side effects to more serious health concerns. “Serious adverse events” is a regulatory term used to describe any medical occurrence that results in death, is life-threatening, requires hospitalization, or causes significant disability.

**Examining the Claim: 1 in 200 Toddlers**

The social media claim refers to data from Moderna’s clinical trials in children aged 6 months to 6 years. According to publicly available summaries of the trial results, a small number of serious adverse events did occur among the thousands of children participating. For example, if 3 serious adverse events occurred among 600 vaccinated children, that would represent roughly 1 in 200 children experiencing such an event.

However, the context is crucial. In vaccine trials, serious adverse events are reported regardless of whether they are related to the vaccine itself. Many such events are determined to be unrelated—for example, accidental injuries, unrelated illnesses, or conditions that occurred by chance during the study period. In Moderna’s trials, the majority of serious adverse events were found to be unrelated to the vaccine as assessed by independent safety monitoring boards.

When reviewing safety, regulatory agencies and vaccine manufacturers distinguish between events temporally associated with the vaccine and those causally linked. If a serious adverse event is judged to be unrelated to the vaccine, it does not count against the safety profile of the vaccine.

**Moderna’s Safety Conclusion**

Despite the low rate of serious adverse events, Moderna and regulatory authorities concluded the vaccine was “safe and effective” for use in young children. This conclusion took into account the totality of the evidence, weighing the benefits of vaccination in preventing COVID-19 (and its potential severe consequences in children) against the risks observed during the trials.

**Conclusion**

The claim that “1 in 200 toddlers” experienced serious adverse events is based on raw numbers but lacks critical nuance. Most reported serious adverse events in the Moderna trial were unrelated to the vaccine. The overall safety assessment by Moderna and regulatory authorities considered both the frequency and the causality of these events. While transparency about trial data is essential, the post misleads by omitting context, potentially overstating the risks associated with the vaccine in young children.

Этот пост усугубляет уже существующие дебаты о безопасности вакцин от коронавируса для маленьких детей. В данной статье мы разберем этот утверждение, предоставим контекст в ходе клинических испытаний и проанализируем, насколько информация точна и представлена объективно.

**Фон по поводу вакцин от коронавируса для детей**

По мере запуска вакцин от коронавируса по всему миру, такие фармацевтические компании, как Moderna, проводили клинические испытания в различных возрастных группах, включая маленьких детей и малышей. Цель этих испытаний заключалась в определении безопасности и эффективности вакцины в профилактике заражения коронавирусом. Вакцина Moderna, как и вакцина Pfizer-BioNTech, использует технологию мРНК для вызова иммунного ответа против коронавируса.

Для получения регуляторного одобрения производители вакцин обязаны мониторить и сообщать о всех нежелательных событиях, произошедших с участниками испытаний, от легких побочных эффектов до более серьезных медицинских проблем. «Серьезные нежелательные события» — это регуляторный термин, который описывает любое медицинское происшествие, приводящее к смерти, представляющее угрозу жизни, требующее госпитализации или вызывающее значительную инвалидность.

**Рассмотрение утверждения: 1 из 200 малышей**

Социальный пост ссылается на данные клинических испытаний Moderna у детей в возрасте от 6 месяцев до 6 лет. Согласно публичным резюме результатов испытаний, в ходе испытаний у тысяч детей действительно произошли небольшое число серьезных нежелательных событий. Например, если 3 серьезных нежелательных события произошли среди 600 вакцинированных детей, это будет означать, что примерно 1 из 200 детей пережил такое событие.

Однако важна контекстуальная информация. В ходе испытаний серьезные нежелательные события сообщаются независимо от того, связаны ли они с самой вакциной или нет. Многие из этих событий оказались несвязанными с вакциной — например, случайные травмы, несвязанные заболевания или состояния, возникшие случайно в течение периода исследования. В испытаниях Moderna большинство серьезных нежелательных событий были признаны несвязанными с вакциной независимыми советами по мониторингу безопасности.

При оценке безопасности регуляторные агентства и производители вакцин различают события, временно связанные с вакциной, и те, которые причинно связаны с ней. Если серьезное нежелательное событие считается несвязанным с вакциной, оно не учитывается в безопасности профиля вакцины.

**Заключение Moderna о безопасности**

Несмотря на низкую частоту серьезных нежелательных событий, Moderna и регуляторные органы пришли к выводу, что вакцина «безопасна и эффективна» для использования у маленьких детей. Этот вывод учитывал весь объем доказательств, взвешивая преимущества вакцинации в предотвращении коронавируса (и его потенциально тяжелых последствий для детей) против рисков, наблюдаемых в ходе испытаний.

**Заключение**

Утверждение, что «1 из 200 малышей» пережили серьезные нежелательные события, основано на сырых цифрах, но не учитывает важную информацию. Большинство сообщенных серьезных нежелательных событий в испытаниях Moderna не было связано с самой вакциной. Общая оценка безопасности, проведенная Moderna и регуляторными органами, учитывала как частоту, так и причинно-следственную связь этих событий. Хотя прозрачность данных о испытаниях важна, пост вводит в заблуждение, исключая контекст, и может преувеличивать риски, связанные с вакциной для маленьких детей.
